request.spec:
A user can watch a person (a toggle on the row, per user; PERSON_WATCHED name=<name>,
PERSON_UNWATCHED name=<name>); show watched yes/no for the signed-in user. When a watched
person's claim is settled, approved or re-settled, one line NOTIFY user=<watcher> person=<name>
number=<number> is written per watching user, in the order they started watching, after the
claim's own line and before the rollup lines.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A user can watch a person (a toggle on the row, per user; PERSON_WATCHED name=<name>,
PERSON_UNWATCHED name=<name>); show watched yes/no for the signed-in user. When a watched
person's claim is settled, approved or re-settled, one line NOTIFY user=<watcher> person=<name>
number=<number> is written per watching user, in the order they started watching, after the

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Watching a person is now in place, and all 4 tests in the spec pass when run with `bin/e2e`.

**What a user sees:** each person's row has a new "Watched" column. It shows `person-watched` as yes/no for whoever is signed in, next to a Watch/Unwatch button (`person-watch`). If watching or unwatching is refused, the reason shows in the row's existing `person-error` element.

**Stored data:** a new migration, `V36__person_watch.sql`, adds a `person_watch` table. It holds one row per person and user, and the row id keeps the order people started watching. Unwatching deletes the row, so someone who starts watching again goes to the back of the order.

**Server:**
- `PUT /api/sheets/{sheet}/people/{id}/watch` takes `{on: true|false}` and writes `PERSON_WATCHED` or `PERSON_UNWATCHED name=<name>`. The button asks for the opposite of what the screen shows. If the user is already in that state (for example, they changed it on another screen), nothing is changed or written.
- Every person view now carries `watched` for the user making the request. That covers the list, edit, retire, hold, add patron and quick-add.
- In `ClaimService`, settling, approving and re-settling each write one `NOTIFY user=<watcher> person=<name> number=<number>` line per watcher, oldest first. The lines come after the claim's own line and before the rollup lines. A clerk's settle that is left PENDING notifies no one. Bulk settle goes through the same code, so it notifies watchers too.

**One choice to check:** a viewer can't watch anyone. The existing guard refuses any change from a viewer, and I left this under that rule. The tests don't cover it, so if viewers should be able to watch, the watch path needs adding to the guard's allowed list.
